title: A phase segment in the hosted machine
statement: Let $K\in\mathbb{N}$, let $Q,T,P_t,P_s$ be types with decidable equality on $P_t,P_s$, and let $R_t$ and $R_s$ be machines on respectively one and $K+1$ work tapes over the record alphabet. Consider a phase $i$ other than the stop phase, configurations $a,b$ for the row machine of phase $i$, a time $t$, and a phase value $v$ such that running that row machine from $a$ for $t$ steps reaches $b$, whose state is $v$. Suppose the phase transition sends $(i,v)$ to a hosted control state $q$, and no state encountered strictly before time $t$ admits a phase transition. If a predicate $B$ holds of all work-head position vectors throughout the row run, including at time $t$, then the hosted machine reaches the state obtained by embedding $b$ in phase $i$ and replacing its phase control by $q$ after $t+1$ steps. Before that final step it visits no state in the stop phase, and $B$ holds of its work-head position vector at every step through $t+1$.
